root_cause.text: In `drivers/scsi/csiostor/csio_scsi.c`, the LUN reset error path could fall through to `CSIO_INC_STATS(rn, n_lun_rst_fail)` even when `rn` was NULL, because the function reused the same `fail` label for both NULL and non-NULL cases, causing a null-pointer dereference in the csiostor SCSI error handler.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes `if (!rn) goto fail;` to `goto fail_ret;` and adds a new `fail_ret:` label after `CSIO_INC_STATS(rn, n_lun_rst_fail)`, matching the commit message that “the error exit path when rn is NULL ends up deferencing the null pointer rn via the use of the macro CSIO_INC_STATS.”

intent_record.intent_summary: Add a dedicated failure return label in the LUN reset handler for clearer error-path control flow.
intent_record.what: A new label `fail_ret:` was inserted immediately before the `return FAILED;` statement in `csio_eh_lun_reset_handler(struct scsi_cmnd *cmnd)`, without changing the return value or surrounding code.
intent_record.how: This adds a reusable fall-through target for existing or future error paths to jump to before returning `FAILED`, but by itself does not alter runtime behavior since execution still ends with the same failure return.
